key_insight: A small number of high-norm "outlier" tokens appear in both the encoder and denoiser of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) and disproportionately attract attention while carrying limited local information; identifying and "taming" these tokens reduces their negative influence on generation.
problem_solved: Outlier tokens in ViT-based diffusion pipelines create attention bottlenecks and degrade image generation quality and stability; the paper diagnoses this phenomenon in RAE–DiT architectures and provides practical ways to mitigate it.
method: Detect outlier tokens by measuring token norms and their attention influence in both the pretrained ViT encoder and the DiT denoiser.
Apply lightweight taming strategies (e.g., per-token norm normalization/clipping, attention reweighting, and regularization) to reduce outlier dominance.
Integrate the taming module into RAE–DiT pipelines with minimal architectural changes and training overhead, evaluating effects on attention patterns and sample quality.
impact: Makes DiT-based image generation more robust and stable by preventing a few tokens from monopolizing attention; practical fixes are easy to plug into existing ViT + diffusion stacks, improving fidelity and interpretability.
visual_elements: Histogram/violin plot of token L2 norms before vs. after taming to show removal/reduction of outliers.
Attention heatmaps from encoder/denoiser illustrating an outlier token attracting excessive attention and the corrected, more distributed attention after taming.
Pipeline diagram of RAE–DiT showing where outlier detection and taming modules plug into the encoder and denoiser.
Side-by-side generated-image comparisons (original vs. tamed) highlighting reduced artifacts and improved local detail.
paper_title: Taming Outlier Tokens in Diffusion Transformers
paper_authors: Xiaoyu Wu, Yifei Wang, Tsu-Jui Fu, Liang-Chieh Chen, Zhe Gan
